newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks start easier, Eurotunnel suspended.
newsitem.headline: French stocks start easier, Eurotunnel suspended.

text.p: French shares opened slightly weaker on Monday on profit-taking ahead of the expiry of September futures contracts this afternoon, dealers said.
Shares in Eurotunnel were suspended at the company's request. The mandate of court-appointed mediators expires today and a source said the mandate would not be extended.

The mediators sought to help arrange a debt deal between the tunnel operator and its banks. The SBF said in a statement that trading in Eurotunnel shares and options was suspended until further notice, pending a statement from the company.
The CAC-40 index was down 2.69 points at 2,104.00.

Eurotunnel has been trying to negotiate a refinancing of more than 62 billion francs in junior-ranked bank debt. It froze interest payments on the bank loans owed to some 225 banks in September last year.
Renault slipped 0.5 percent to 121.30 despite the company chairman's remark on Sunday that he expected the group to show record September car sales in France.
Canal Plus fell 1.35 percent in limited turnover. The share made big gains last week and some investors are taking profits.
